translations.t_about_msg_001:
ZFSMgr
Cross-platform ZFS manager.
Author: Eladio Linares
License: GNU
translations.t_admite_nativas: It also accepts the original command's flags. Short ones with no value can be grouped, as in OpenZFS: «-wLec» is «-w -L -e -c».
translations.t_ak_det1: It goes «from where I am, over there»: it takes the public key of the machine you are on —or the one in «--on»— and adds it to the `authorized_keys` of the one you name. After that, the first can log into the second without a password.
translations.t_ak_det2: It is idempotent: if the key is already there, it is not duplicated.
translations.t_ak_det3: This does NOT go through the daemon, and it cannot: it is what has to be done BEFORE there is a daemon, because «install-daemon» needs to get in over SSH. That is why it is one of the few commands still sending shell.

translations.t_bd_det1: The arguments go in PAIRS: each subdirectory with the name of the dataset that replaces it. From the outside nothing moves: where there was a directory there is now a dataset with the same contents, and with its own properties, snapshots and quota.
translations.t_bd_det2: The name does NOT have to mirror the path: creating a dataset only requires its parent to exist by name, so `breakdown a/b/c a:b:c` converts the three-level one without converting `a` or `b`.
translations.t_bd_det3: Every byte moves ONCE and the originals are deleted at the end, once every copy is verified: if something fails midway, the original is still intact. That is why it is worth leaving it as a JOB —without --wait— when there is volume: follow it with «job <id>» and the interpreter stays free.
translations.t_bd_det4:
Example, standing on zfsm://local/tank/media:
  breakdown fotos fotos videos videos
leaves tank/media/fotos and tank/media/videos where two directories were.

translations.t_carga_la_c_0013a3: Load the encryption key. The passphrase is typed in.
translations.t_ck_det1: The passphrase NEVER travels as an argument: it would sit in the process's argv and be visible with `ps` on both machines. It goes encrypted inside the request to the daemon, which hands it to `zfs change-key` on standard input.
translations.t_ck_det2: The dataset must have its key LOADED: on a locked one, `zfs` cannot change anything. If needed, «load-key» first.
translations.t_ck_det3: It changes THIS dataset's passphrase. Those inheriting its key keep inheriting it; nothing else is needed for that.
translations.t_ck_fd_q: The new passphrase, through a file descriptor. Without it, it is typed in, and asked twice.
translations.t_ck_res: Changes the passphrase of an encrypted dataset.
translations.t_clear_det: It ASKS first, even though it destroys no data: people type `clear` meaning to clear the terminal, and then a pool's error count —the very thing they were looking at— is lost without being asked for. To clear the screen, «cls».
translations.t_clone_det1: A RELATIVE name hangs off the snapshot's dataset: standing on `tank/datos@ayer`, «clone copia» leaves `tank/datos/copia`. To put it elsewhere give the full ZFS name: «clone tank/copia».
translations.t_clone_det2: The clone shares blocks with the snapshot, so at first it takes up almost nothing — and that snapshot CANNOT be destroyed while the clone exists. «promote» breaks that tie.
translations.t_clone_det3:
Example:
  cd /local/tank/datos@ayer
  clone recuperado
or from anywhere: «clone tank/recuperado --from /local/tank/datos@ayer».
translations.t_clone_dst_req001: The target dataset cannot be empty.
translations.t_clone_need_sel001:

translations.t_clone_same_pool1: Clone requires Source and Target to be in the same pool.
translations.t_cls_det: It is called «cls» and not «clear» because `clear` already exists and belongs to the pool: it resets its error counters. Typing `clear` meaning to clear the terminal is easy and was not harmless, so that one asks first.

translations.t_edit_det_local: On the LOCAL connection, this is what changes this machine's sudo credentials: «edit local --user <u> --password». They are checked on the spot —if they do not elevate, it says so— and what the session had remembered is refreshed, including the TLS material that was read by elevating with the previous password. Without that, the change seemed to have no effect until leaving and coming back.

translations.t_peers_det1: Needed to LEVEL a schedule against another machine: the daemon does that on its own, at night and with nobody in front, so the credentials have to be on the machine and not on your laptop.
translations.t_peers_det2: It is handed, per connection, where to reach it and THAT machine's TLS material: each daemon verifies its clients against its own certificate, so to talk to one you must present its own. It is the same thing the client's trust store keeps.
translations.t_peers_det3: It travels encrypted inside the request and lands in a root-owned file with mode 600: it carries PRIVATE KEYS. Whoever can read it can impersonate this machine to the others, so you are asked before sending it.
translations.t_peers_det4: «--listen» is needed on the machine that RECEIVES a levelling: by default the daemon only answers on 127.0.0.1, and only the client gets there because it opens an SSH tunnel — at night there is nobody to open it. Only a wildcard is accepted: tying it to a single address would cut off the client itself, which comes in through the tunnel.
translations.t_peers_det5: With the wildcard, the daemon's port becomes reachable from the network, protected by mTLS with a PINNED client certificate. It is not new exposure: the transfer port already listens on every interface with a one-time token, and is less protected than this one.

translations.t_uso_s_opci_010447:
Usage: %s [options] <command>

With no command it enters INTERACTIVE MODE: a shell where the location
is a zfsm:// URL and every command acts on it.

Commands:
  (none)                Interactive mode, starting at zfsm://Local
  connections list      Lists the configured connections
  url parse <zfsm://…>  Parses a URL and shows what it names
  version               This tool's version

Options:
  --password-fd <n>     Read the master password from that descriptor.
                        Without it, it is asked for on the terminal.
  --config-dir <path>   Configuration directory (by default,
                        ~/.config/ZFSMgr)
  --no-secrets          Decrypts nothing: does not ask for a master password.
                        Encrypted fields come out as <cifrado>.
  --format text|tsv|json
                        text (the default) is for reading; tsv is for
                        scripts: no header, tabs, fixed columns
                        in English and «-» where there is no value, just
                        like `zfs list -H`; json is for programs:
                        numbers come out as numbers, booleans as
                        booleans and what does not apply as null.
                        connections list: id, name, type, os, user,
                        host, port, sudo, tls, connected
  --url <zfsm://…>      Where to start in interactive mode
  -v, --verbose         Reports on standard error what the transport
                        does with each machine
  -y, --yes             Do not ask before destructive actions
  -h, --help            This help

The master password is NOT passed as an argument or an environment
variable: both are visible in `ps` to any user of the machine. With the
descriptor any secret manager can be used:

  %s --password-fd 3 connections list  3< <(pass show zfsmgr)
